content.text: {"quote_faithful":"yes","verdict":"rejected","evidence_kind":"missing_justification","fatal":"no","explanation":"The quoted wording is imprecise in calling (4) “symmetric,” but the required operation is valid and sufficiently indicated. Since (4) holds for every ordered pair x,y, it may be reapplied with x chosen from the e-orbit and y from the c-orbit. The write-up explicitly clarifies this in the irrational case: “replace x by y, which swaps c and e,” and gives the resulting negative coefficient 4e(e-c). The identical relabelling applies in the rational case. Thus no symmetry of the algebraic expression itself is required, and the objection identifies at most a presentational imprecision, not a missing mathematical step."}
